QUSHAYRI:v3p347/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p347/r8.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p347/r8.claim: At judgment every person is exposed and held to account, receiving rebuke or punishment according to what is due.
QUSHAYRI:v3p347/r8.anchor: وفي كل نفس مع هؤلاء القوم محاسبة ومطالبة

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p445/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p445/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p445/r7.claim: Verses 13–18 portray the terrors of the Day of Judgement.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p445/r7.anchor: a portrayal of the horrors of the Day of Judgement.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p453/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p453/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p453/r2.claim: Being brought forth means before God; after the heavens and earth are destroyed, no place or thing can hide a person.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p453/r2.anchor: the heavens and the earth shall be destroyed; so a person will not have any place to hide himself

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r1.claim: On that day people are exposed for reckoning; the phrase answers the first conditional, with the day broad enough to include what follows the first blast, or directly marking the second blast.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r1.anchor: يومئذ: أي يوم إذ كان ما ذكر، تعرضون: أي للحساب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r2.claim: The address in tuʿraḍūn covers all who are subject to reckoning; the timing clauses can be read as a substitution within the Resurrection-day setting.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r2.anchor: والخطاب في تعرضون لجميع العالم المحاسبين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r3.speaker: عبد الله
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r3.claim: A report from ʿAbd Allāh says Moses sees two presentations at Resurrection involving excuses, reprimands, and disputes, followed by a third in which records fly to right and left.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r3.anchor: وعن عبد الله: رأى موسى في القيامة عرضتان فيهما معاذير وتوقيف وخصومات

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r4.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r4.claim: Most readers use the feminine verb lā takhfā; ʿAlī and several others read the masculine lā yakhfā.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r4.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: لا تخفى بتاء التأنيث وعلي وابن وثاب وطلحة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r5.claim: Khāfiyah refers to an inner secret or a condition that had been hidden in worldly life.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p259/r5.anchor: خافية: سريرة وحال كانت تخفى في الدنيا

SAMIN-DURR:69:18/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:69:18/r1.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:69:18/r1.claim: The Shaykh takes تعرضون as the answer to إذا in فإذا نفخ.
SAMIN-DURR:69:18/r1.anchor: قوله: { يومئذ تعرضون }: " تعرضون " هو جواب " إذا "

SAMIN-DURR:69:18/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:69:18/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:69:18/r2.claim: Al-Samin says the answer to إذا is وقع الواقعة; تعرضون is a new independent sentence.
SAMIN-DURR:69:18/r2.anchor: بل جوابها ما تقدم من قوله " وقعت الواقعة " و " تعرضون " على هذا مستأنف

SAMIN-DURR:69:18/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:69:18/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:69:18/r3.claim: The two readers read feminine ياء, justified by nonliteral gender and separation; others use تاء for overt feminine marking, the default.
SAMIN-DURR:69:18/r3.anchor: قرأ الأخوان بالياء من تحت؛ لأن التأنيث مجازي، وللفصل أيضا

SAMIN-DURR:69:18/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:69:18/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:69:18/r4.claim: The rest read لا تخفى with تاء for overt feminine marking and the original vowel opening.
SAMIN-DURR:69:18/r4.anchor: والباقون " لا تخفى " بالتاء من فوق للتأنيث اللفظي، والفتح وهو الأصل

SAMIN-DURR:69:18/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:69:18/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:69:18/r5.claim: واهية means weak; the verb وهى means to weaken, and a water skin described as واهى is torn; the poem witnesses وهى.
SAMIN-DURR:69:18/r5.anchor: أي: ضعيفة. يقال: وهى الشيء يهي وهيا، أي: ضعف ووهى السقاء: انخرق

SAMIN-DURR:69:18/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:69:18/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:69:18/r6.claim: أرجائها means its sides or regions; the singular رجا has a short alif written against the pattern of رمى, as رجوان and the cited poetry show.
SAMIN-DURR:69:18/r6.anchor: أي: جوانبها ونواحيها. واحدها: رجا بالقصر، يكتب الألف عكس رمى

ASAD-NOTES:69:18/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:69:18/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:69:18/r1.claim: At judgment every person is exposed, and not even the most hidden deed remains concealed.
ASAD-NOTES:69:18/r1.anchor: not [even] the most hidden of your deeds will remain hidden

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p351#2/r1.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p351#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p351#2/r1.claim: لا تخفى منكم خافية is read with either yāʾ or tāʾ; no reader attribution or rationale is given here.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p351#2/r1.anchor: يقرأ بالياء والتاء فأما قوله خافية فقيل أراد نفس خافية

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p351#2/r2.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p351#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p351#2/r2.claim: One reported interpretation takes خافية to mean a hidden person or soul.
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p351#2/r2.anchor: فأما قوله خافية فقيل أراد نفس خافية

IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p351#2/r3.author: Ibn Khālawayh (attr.)
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p351#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKHALAWAYH-HUJJA:v1p351#2/r3.claim: Another reported interpretation takes خافية to mean a hidden act.

QIRAAT-ER:69:18:4#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:69:18:4#1/r1.speaker: Imp
QIRAAT-ER:69:18:4#1/r1.claim: The Imp form yakhfī is masculine singular instead of feminine takhfā; it can make Allāh the implicit subject: He will hide no secret from you.
QIRAAT-ER:69:18:4#1/r1.anchor: Masculine 3rd person singular yakhfī instead of feminine takhfā — verb becomes masculine

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p314/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p314/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p314/r1.claim: Qatāda says people are presented three times: the first two involve disputes and excuses, while the third is when records fly into their hands.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p314/r1.anchor: عن معمر عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ تعرضون لا تخفى منكم خافية ﴾ قال تعرضون ثلاث عرضات فأما عرضتان ففيهما الخصومات والمعاذير

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p314/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p314/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p314/r2.claim: Qatāda tentatively reports that a wife asked whether people remember their families at Judgment; the Prophet says not at the scales, the bridge, or when records fly into hands.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p314/r2.anchor: عن معمر عن قتادة قال سئل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أحسبة قال سأله بعض أزواجه هل يذكر الناس أهليهم يوم القيامة

ALUSI-FULL:v29p46/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p46/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p46/r1.claim: The presentation is a metaphor for being called to account, likened to a ruler reviewing an army to inspect their condition.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p46/r1.anchor: مجازا عن الحساب والمراد يومئذ تحاسبون لكنه شبه ذلك بعرض السلطان العسكر

ALUSI-FULL:v29p46/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p46/r2.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v29p46/r2.claim: Abu Musa reports the Prophet saying people are presented three times on Judgment Day: two for disputing and excuses, and a third when records fly into right and left hands; no grading is stated.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p46/r2.anchor: عن أبي موسى قال قال رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم يعرض الناس يوم القيامة ثلاث عرضات

ALUSI-FULL:v29p46/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p46/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p46/r3.claim: The implied sentence replaced by the tanwīn is the blowing of the trumpet; yawmʾidhin yuʿraḍūn substitutes for the preceding time phrase, within an expansive sequence of events.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p46/r3.anchor: والجملة المعوض عنها التنوين على ما يدل عليه كلامهم نفخ في الصور وجعل يومئذ تعرضون بدلا من فيومئذ

ALUSI-FULL:v29p46/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p46/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p46/r4.claim: The clause lā takhfā minkum khāfiyah is circumstantial to the subject of tuʿraḍūn.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p46/r4.anchor: حال من مرفوع تعرضون أي تعرضون غير خاف عليه عز وجل سر من أسراركم

ALUSI-FULL:v29p46/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p46/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p46/r5.claim: No secret is hidden from God even before the presentation; it exposes people's state, establishes proof, and displays perfect justice.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p46/r5.anchor: أي تعرضون غير خاف عليه عز وجل سر من أسراركم قبل ذلك أيضا وإنما العرض لإفشاء الحال وإقامة الحجة والمبالغة في العدل

ALUSI-FULL:v29p46/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p46/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v29p46/r6.claim: Alternatively, nothing can be hidden from people on that day, as in the verse about secrets being tested and exposed.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p46/r6.anchor: أو غير خاف يومئذ على الناس كقوله تعالى يوم تبلى السرائر

ALUSI-FULL:v29p46/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p46/r7.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وابن وثاب وطلحة والأعمش وابن مقسم عن عاصم
ALUSI-FULL:v29p46/r7.claim: These readers and others read the verb with masculine yāʾ: lā yakhfā.
ALUSI-FULL:v29p46/r7.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي وابن وثاب وطلحة والأعمش وابن مقسم عن عاصم وغيرهم لا يخفى بالياء التحتانية

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p211/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p211/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p211/r1.claim: On that Day people are presented before God.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p211/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p211/r2.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p211/r2.claim: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read masculine singular with yāʾ; other readers use feminine with tāʾ.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p211/r2.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي: "لا يخفى" بالياء، وقرأ الآخرون بالتاء

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p211/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p211/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p211/r3.anchor: منكم خافية} أي فعلة خافية. قال الكلبي:

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p211/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p211/r4.speaker: الكلبي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p211/r4.claim: Al-Kalbī says nothing about people is hidden from God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p211/r4.anchor: لا يخفى على الله منكم شيء. قال أبو موسى:

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p211/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p211/r5.speaker: أبو موسى
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p211/r5.claim: Abū Mūsā says people undergo three presentations: first disputation and excuses, then books scatter and each takes one in the right or left hand.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p211/r5.anchor: قال أبو موسى: يعرض الناس ثلاث عرضات، فأما عرضتان فجدال ومعاذير وأما العرضة الثالثة فعندها تطاير الصحف

BAYDAWI-FULL:69:18-19/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:18-19/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:18-19/r1.claim: The reckoning is likened to a ruler displaying troops to inspect their condition.
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:18-19/r1.anchor: تشبيها للمحاسبة بعرض السلطان العسكر لتعرف أحوالهم

BAYDAWI-FULL:69:18-19/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:18-19/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:18-19/r2.claim: Although this follows the second blast, the modifier 'that Day' can cover the extended time containing both blasts, the swoon, resurrection, reckoning, and entry into Paradise or the Fire.
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:18-19/r2.anchor: لما كان اليوم اسما لزمان متسع تقع فيه النفختان والصعقة والنشور والحساب

BAYDAWI-FULL:69:18-19/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:18-19/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:18-19/r3.claim: No secret is hidden from God; the display is to disclose people's condition and make justice manifest, not to inform God.
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:18-19/r3.anchor: سريرة على الله تعالى حتى يكون العرض للاطلاع عليها

BAYDAWI-FULL:69:18-19/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:18-19/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:18-19/r4.claim: Alternatively, nothing is hidden from people, as in the verse about secrets being tested.
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:18-19/r4.anchor: أو على الناس كما قال الله تعالى

BAYDAWI-FULL:69:18-19/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:18-19/r5.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
BAYDAWI-FULL:69:18-19/r5.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read the verb with yāʾ, with the separation as the reason given.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p128/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p128/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p128/r6.claim: Biqāʿī moves from warning about the Day of Calling to its general scene, the presentation, and then its particular division between beneficent and sinful people.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p128/r6.anchor: فالعامة العرض , والخاصة التقسيم إلى محسن ومسيء

BIQAI-FULL:v8p128/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p128/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p128/r7.claim: The phrase means on that day, when the events just described have taken place.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p128/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p128/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p128/r8.claim: The verb is passive because the presentation itself is terrifying and because the statement comes from the Almighty.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p128/r8.anchor: ولما كان المهول نفس العرض , بنى فعله للمفعول ولأنه كلام القادرين

BIQAI-FULL:v8p128/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p128/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p128/r9.claim: Being presented to God for account is likened to a ruler reviewing troops to select the good for honor, nearness, and reward, and the corrupt for removal and punishment; the part stands for the whole accounting.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p128/r9.anchor: كما يعرض السلطان الجند لينظر في أمرهم ليختار منهم المصلح للإكرام والتقريب والإثابة

BIQAI-FULL:v8p128/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p128/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p128/r10.claim: Nothing about anyone is hidden from anyone that day, neither deeds nor selves, however subtle; complete disclosure from graves and hearts magnifies the saved person's happiness and the wicked person's misery.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p128/r10.anchor: أي في ذلك اليوم على أحد بوجه من الوجوه الخفاء في الدنيا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p128/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p128/r11.speaker: أبو موسى رضي الله عنه
BIQAI-FULL:v8p128/r11.claim: Abū Mūsā says there are three presentations: the first two involve disputation and excuses, while at the third the records fly out and people take them in the right or left hand.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p128/r11.anchor: قال أبو موسى رضي الله عنه : هي ثلاث عرضات فأما عرضتان فجدال ومعاذير

DURR-FULL:v8p270/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p270/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p270/r2.claim: Qatāda says people are presented three times: the first two involve disputes and excuses, while the third sees the records fly into their hands.
DURR-FULL:v8p270/r2.anchor: تعرضون ثلاث عرضات فأما عرضتان ففيهما الخصومات والمعاذير وأما الثالثة فتطاير الصحف في الأيدي

DURR-FULL:v8p270/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p270/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p270/r3.claim: A report from Qatāda says the Prophet described three presentations: disputes, excuses, and argument in the first two, then books flying into hands in the third; he prayed for right-hand recipients.
DURR-FULL:v8p270/r3.anchor: عن قتادة {يومئذ تعرضون لا تخفى منكم خافية} قال: ذكر لنا أن نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقول: تعرض الناس ثلاث عرضات يوم القيامة فأما عرضتان ففيهما خصومات ومعاذير وجدال

DURR-FULL:v8p270/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p270/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p270/r6.claim: Abū Mūsā reports the Prophet's account of three presentations: debate and excuses in the first two, then each person's record in the right or left hand in the third.
DURR-FULL:v8p270/r6.anchor: عن أبي موسى قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: يعرض الناس يوم القيامة ثلاث عرضات فأما عرضتان فجدال ومعاذير

DURR-FULL:v8p270/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p270/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p270/r7.claim: In an explanation of this verse, the Prophet is reported to describe two presentations of dispute followed by a third when the records fly into people's hands.
DURR-FULL:v8p270/r7.anchor: في قوله: {يومئذ تعرضون لا تخفى منكم خافية} قال: عرضتان فيهما الخصومة والجدال

DURR-FULL:v8p270/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p270/r8.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v8p270/r8.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says the first two presentations involve argument and excuses, while books fly into right and left hands in the third.
DURR-FULL:v8p270/r8.anchor: عن ابن مسعد قال: يعرض الناس يوم القيامة ثلاث عرضات فأما عرضتان فجدال ومعاذير وأما العرضة الثالثة فتطاير الكتب بالأيمان والشمائل

DURR-FULL:v8p271/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p271/r1.speaker: عمر
DURR-FULL:v8p271/r1.claim: ʿUmar urges people to take account of themselves before being judged, weigh themselves before being weighed, and prepare for the great presentation.
DURR-FULL:v8p271/r1.anchor: عن عمر قال: حاسبوا أنفسكم قبل أن تحاسبوا فإنه أيسر لحسابكم وزنوا أنفسكم قبل أن توزنوا وتجهزوا للعرض الأكبر

DURR-FULL:v8p271/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p271/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v8p271/r4.claim: The Prophet says he will recognize his community by the marks of ablution, their records in their right hands, and their light ahead of them.
DURR-FULL:v8p271/r4.anchor: عن أبي الدرداء قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: إنا أول من يؤذن له في السجود يوم القيامة وأنا أول من يؤذن له أن يرفع رأسه

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3371/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3371/r1.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3371/r1.claim: Abu Musa reports the Prophet saying people will be presented three times: twice for disputation and excuses, then when the books fly into their hands and they take them with the right or left.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3371/r1.anchor: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ' يعرض الناس يوم القيامة ثلاث عرضات فاما عرضتان فجدال ومعاذير ، واما الثالثة فعند ذلك تطاير الصحف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p128/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p128/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p128/r10.claim: “You will be presented” addresses all people, as the context and the following details show.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p128/r10.anchor: والخطاب في قوله : { تعرضون } لجميع الناس بقرينة المقام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p128/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p128/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p128/r11.claim: ʿArḍ originally means passing things before someone for inspection, like merchandise before a buyer or troops before a commander; here it alludes to reckoning, while the literal sense may also apply.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p128/r11.anchor: والعرض : أصله إمرار الأشياء على من يريد التأمل منها مثل عرض السلعة على المشتري

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p128/r12.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p128/r12.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p128/r12.claim: No hidden thing is concealed from God or His angels.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p128/r12.anchor: لا تخفى على الله ولا على ملائكته

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p128/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p128/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p128/r13.claim: The feminine khafiya may describe an implicit feminine act, or a soul/person: no one can hide from the accounting.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p128/r13.anchor: وتأنيث { خافية } لأنه وصف لموصوف مؤنث يقدر بالفعلة من أفعال العباد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p128/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p128/r14.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p128/r14.claim: At judgment no one is hidden and no confusion remains between believer and unbeliever or virtuous and wicked.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p128/r14.anchor: ولا يلتبس كافر بمؤمن ، ولا بار بفاجر .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p129/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p129/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p129/r1.claim: The clause may stand independently, explain the preceding event, or serve as its بدل اشتمال.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p129/r1.anchor: وجملة { يومئذ تعرضون } مستأنفة ، أو هي بيان لجملة { فيومئذ وقعت الواقعة ، } أو بدل اشتمال منها .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p129/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p129/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p129/r2.claim: منكم qualifies خافية but is fronted, making it a circumstantial phrase.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p129/r2.anchor: و { منكم } صفة ل { خافية } قدمت عليه فتكون حالا .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p129/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p129/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p129/r3.claim: Repeating يومئذ four times magnifies the terror of the day, whose events begin with the trumpet blast.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p129/r3.anchor: وتكرير { يومئذ } أربع مرات لتهويل ذلك اليوم الذي مبدؤه النفخ في الصور

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p129/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p129/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p129/r4.claim: The day is mentioned five times overall: the first يومئذ repeats إذا in the trumpet-blast clause, followed by four repetitions.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p129/r4.anchor: فقد جرى ذكر ذلك اليوم خمس مرات لأن { فيومئذ وقعت الواقعة } تكرير ل ( إذا ) من قوله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p129/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p129/r5.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p129/r5.claim: The majority read تخفى with feminine ت; the feminine subject خافية follows a gap and is nonhuman/non-natural feminine.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p129/r5.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { لا تخفى } بمثناة فوقية .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p129/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p129/r6.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وخلف
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p129/r6.claim: Hamza, al-Kisa'i, and Khalaf read تخفى with ي because خافية is not naturally feminine and is separated from its verb.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p129/r6.anchor: وقرأه حمزة والكسائي وخلف بالتحتية لأن تأنيث { خافية } غير حقيقي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p129/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p129/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p129/r7.claim: The presentation is presentation for reckoning and recompense, which introduces the detailed account of people's outcomes.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p129/r7.anchor: الفاء تفصيل لما يتضمنه { تعرضون } ( الحاقة : 18 ) إذ العرض عرض للحساب والجزاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p350/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p350/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p350/r5.claim: On Judgment Day people will be presented to God for their reckoning, and no person or deed will be hidden from Him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p350/r5.anchor: قوله تعالى يومئذ تعرضون على الله لحسابكم لا تخفى عليه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p350/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p350/r6.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p350/r6.claim: Hamza and al-Kisai read the verb with yāʾ, while the other readers use tāʾ.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p350/r6.anchor: قرأ حمزة والكسائي لا يخفى بالياء وقرأ الباقون بالتاء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p350/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p350/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p350/r7.claim: The meaning is that no hidden person or hidden deed among them escapes God.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p350/r7.anchor: والمعنى لا يخفى عليه منكم خافية أي نفس خافية أو فعلة خافية

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p350/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p350/r8.speaker: أبو موسى
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p350/r8.claim: The Prophet says people will be presented three times: the first two involve argument and excuses, and at the third the records fly into their hands, with some receiving the right hand and others the left.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p350/r8.anchor: وفي حديث أبي موسى عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قال يعرض الناس يوم القيامة ثلاث عرضات

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p350/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p350/r9.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p350/r9.claim: Umar urged people to take account of themselves before being judged, weigh themselves before being weighed, and prepare for the great presentation.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p350/r9.anchor: وكان عمر بن الخطاب يقول حاسبوا أنفسكم قل أن تحاسبوا وزنوها قبل أن توزنوا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p212#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p212#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p212#2/r2.claim: On that day people are presented before the Knower of secrets and private counsel, who knows their outward and inward states and innermost thoughts.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p212#2/r2.anchor: أي تعرضون على عالم السر والنجوى الذي لا يخفى عليه شيء من أموركم، بل هو عالم بالظواهر والسرائر والضمائر؛ ولهذا قال: {لا تخفى منكم خافية}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p212#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p212#2/r3.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p212#2/r3.claim: Umar urges people to audit themselves before judgment, weigh themselves before being weighed, and prepare for the great presentation, citing this verse.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p212#2/r3.anchor: قال عمر بن الخطاب، رضي الله عنه: حاسبوا أنفسكم قبل أن تحاسبوا، وزنوا أنفسكم قبل أن توزنوا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p212#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p212#2/r4.speaker: أبو موسى
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p212#2/r4.claim: The Prophet says people face three presentations on Judgment Day: two for disputation and excuses, then records fly into hands, with each person receiving a record in the right or left; al-Tirmidhi gives Abu Hurayra instead of Abu Musa as the Companion narrator.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p212#2/r4.anchor: عن أبي موسى قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "يعرض الناس يوم القيامة ثلاث عرضات، فأما عرضتان فجدال ومعاذير

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p212#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p212#2/r5.speaker: عبد الله
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p212#2/r5.claim: Ibn Masud likewise reports three presentations: two for excuses and disputes, then the records fly into people's hands; Qatada transmits a similar report as a mursal narration.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p212#2/r5.anchor: عن عبد الله قال: يعرض الناس يوم القيامة ثلاث عرضات: عرضتان، معاذير وخصومات، والعرضة الثالثة تطير الصحف في الأيدي.

BURSEVI:v10p106/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p106/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p106/r3.claim: The verb “you are presented” governs “that day”; presentation means being brought before God for questioning and accounting, like a ruler reviewing troops, and the address covers everyone by predominance.
BURSEVI:v10p106/r3.anchor: على الله أي تسألون وتحاسبون عبر عنه بذلك تشبيها له بعرض السلطان العسكر

BURSEVI:v10p106/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p106/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p106/r4.claim: A report describes three presentations on Judgment Day: two involve excuses, arguments, and rebuke, while the third distributes the records, with the successful receiving their book in the right hand and the doomed in the left.
BURSEVI:v10p106/r4.anchor: أن في يوم القيامة ثلاث عرضات فأما عرضتان فاعتذار واحتجاج وتوبيخ

BURSEVI:v10p106/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p106/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p106/r5.claim: Although presentation follows the second trumpet, “the Day” spans the trumpet blasts, swoon, resurrection, reckoning, and entry into Paradise or Hell, so it can serve as the time for them all.
BURSEVI:v10p106/r5.anchor: لكن لما كان اليوماسما لزمان متسع يقع فيه النفختان والصعقة والنشور

BURSEVI:v10p106/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p106/r6.speaker: المشبهة
BURSEVI:v10p106/r6.claim: The anthropomorphists take the references to the Throne's bearing and the presentation to mean that God is carried and present on the Throne.
BURSEVI:v10p106/r6.anchor: وذهب المشبهة من حمل العرش والعرض إلى كونه تعالى محمولا حاضرا في العرش

BURSEVI:v10p106/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p106/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p106/r7.claim: The author replies that the imagery depicts God's majesty by comparison with rulers presiding over judgment; God's coming amid clouds means the coming of His command and decree.
BURSEVI:v10p106/r7.anchor: وأجيب بأنه تمثل لعظمة الله بما يشاهد من أحوال السلاطين يوم بروزهم للقضاء العام

BURSEVI:v10p106/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p106/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p106/r8.claim: The author interprets the report of transformation as God's manifestation in an attribute-rank; the Prophet's vision of a beardless youth during the Ascension is like a dream vision, since God is exalted beyond bodily qualities.
BURSEVI:v10p106/r8.anchor: وأما حديث التحول فمحمول على ظهوره تعالى في مرتبة الصفت ولا مناقشة فيه لأن النبي عليه اسلام رآه ليلة المعراج في صورة شاب امرد

BURSEVI:v10p106/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p106/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p106/r9.claim: The final clause is circumstantial to “you are presented”; min-kum originally modified khāfiya but was fronted for the rhyme, and it syntactically reaches both the preceding and following wording.
BURSEVI:v10p106/r9.anchor: حال من مرفوع تعرضون ومنكم كان في الأصل صفة لخافية قدم للفاصلة

BURSEVI:v10p106/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p106/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p106/r10.claim: Presentation exposes every hidden secret and displays the state to emphasize justice; the source compares it with 82:9, “the day the secrets are tested.”
BURSEVI:v10p106/r10.anchor: أي تعرضون غير خاف عليه تعالى فعلة خفيفة أي سر من أسراركم وإنما العرض لإفشاء الحال والمبالغة في العدل

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p80#2/r22.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p80#2/r22.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p80#2/r22.claim: The presentation takes place on the Day of Resurrection.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p80#2/r23.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p80#2/r23.speaker: النبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p80#2/r23.claim: The Prophet, through al-Hasan from Abu Musa, says people are presented three times: two for disputation and excuses, then their books fly into their hands for reception in the right or left.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p80#2/r23.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( يعرض الناس يوم القيامة ثلاث عرضات

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p80#2/r24.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p80#2/r24.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p80#2/r24.claim: ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAs explains that believers will be distinguishable from disbelievers, and the righteous from the wicked.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p80#2/r24.anchor: لا يخفى المؤمن من الكافر , ولا البر من الفاجر , قاله عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p80#2/r25.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p80#2/r25.speaker: النبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p80#2/r25.claim: The Prophet says people will be gathered barefoot and naked, so no private parts will be concealed.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p80#2/r25.anchor: لا تستتر منكم عورة , كما قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( يحشر الناس حفاة عراة )

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p80#2/r26.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p80#2/r26.speaker: ابن شجرة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p80#2/r26.claim: Ibn Shajara takes khāfiya to mean a hidden deed people used to conceal.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p80#2/r26.anchor: أن خافية بمعنى خفية كانوا يخفونها من أعمالهم حكاه ابن شجرة

MUQATIL:69:13-18/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:69:13-18/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:69:13-18/r8.claim: People are presented before God for reckoning according to their deeds.

MUQATIL:69:13-18/r9.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:69:13-18/r9.speaker: author
MUQATIL:69:13-18/r9.claim: Neither the righteous nor the wicked are concealed when presented.
MUQATIL:69:13-18/r9.anchor: { لا تخفى منكم خافية } [آية: 18] يقول: لا يخفى الصالح منكم، ولا الطالح إذا عرضتم

NASAFI-FULL:v4p275#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p275#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p275#5/r1.claim: Being presented means being brought for reckoning and questioning, like a ruler reviewing an army to inspect its condition.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p275#5/r1.anchor: للحساب والسؤال شبه ذلك بعرض السلطان العسكر لتعرف أحواله

NASAFI-FULL:v4p275#5/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p275#5/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p275#5/r2.claim: Nothing hidden in worldly life remains hidden: neither inner secrets nor any state.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p275#5/r2.anchor: سريرة وحال كانت تخفى في الدنيا

NASAFI-FULL:v4p275#5/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p275#5/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p275#5/r3.claim: The Kufans other than ʿĀṣim read the verb with yāʾ.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p275#5/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p275#5/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
NASAFI-FULL:v4p275#5/r4.claim: The Prophet said people are presented three times on Resurrection Day: the first two are for argument and excuses; at the third, records fly, and the saved take theirs in the right hand and the doomed in the left.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p275#5/r4.anchor: وفي الحديث يعرض الناس يوم القيامة ثلاث عرضات فأما عرضتان فجدال ومعاذير وأما الثالثة فعندها تطيرا الصحف

QURTUBI-FULL:69:18/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:18/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:69:18/r1.claim: Being presented before God means facing the reckoning and having deeds laid out for recompense, not informing God of something He did not know; Qurtubi cites 18:48 as a parallel.
QURTUBI-FULL:69:18/r1.anchor: ليس ذلك عرضا يعلم به ما لم يكن عالما به، بل معناه الحساب وتقرير الأعمال عليهم للمجازاة

QURTUBI-FULL:69:18/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:18/r2.speaker: أبو هريرة
QURTUBI-FULL:69:18/r2.claim: Al-Hasan transmits from Abu Hurayra that people face three presentations at Resurrection: two for dispute and excuses, then records fly into their hands, right or left. Tirmidhi says it is unsound because al-Hasan did not hear from Abu Hurayra.
QURTUBI-FULL:69:18/r2.anchor: روى الحسن عن أبي هريرة قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

QURTUBI-FULL:69:18/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:18/r3.speaker: ابن شجرة
QURTUBI-FULL:69:18/r3.claim: Ibn Shajara explains that God knows every deed, including things people tried to conceal; khafiya means a hidden act.
QURTUBI-FULL:69:18/r3.anchor: ف «خافية» على هذا بمعنى خفية، كانوا يخفونها من أعمالهم قاله ابن شجرة

QURTUBI-FULL:69:18/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:18/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:69:18/r4.claim: Another explanation is that no person escapes notice or remains unjudged.
QURTUBI-FULL:69:18/r4.anchor: وقيل: لا يخفى عليه إنسان أي لا يبقى إنسان لا يحاسب

QURTUBI-FULL:69:18/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:18/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
QURTUBI-FULL:69:18/r5.claim: Abd Allah ibn ʿAmr says believers will be distinguishable from disbelievers and the righteous from the wicked.
QURTUBI-FULL:69:18/r5.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص: لا يخفى المؤمن من الكافر

QURTUBI-FULL:69:18/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:18/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:69:18/r6.claim: A further interpretation is that no nakedness will remain covered, in light of the report that people are resurrected barefoot and naked.

QURTUBI-FULL:69:18/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:18/r7.speaker: الكوفيون إلا عاصما
QURTUBI-FULL:69:18/r7.claim: The Kufans except ʿAsim read the verb in the masculine, la yakhfa, because khafiya is grammatically feminine but not feminine in sense; Abu ʿUbayd prefers this reading because the prepositional phrase separates verb and subject.
QURTUBI-FULL:69:18/r7.anchor: وقرأ الكوفيون إلا عاصما «لا يخفى» بالياء لأن تأنيث الخافية غير حقيقي

QURTUBI-FULL:69:18/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:69:18/r8.speaker: الباقون
QURTUBI-FULL:69:18/r8.claim: The other readers use the feminine verb, la takhfa; Abu Hatim prefers it because the subject khafiya is feminine.
QURTUBI-FULL:69:18/r8.anchor: الباقون بالتاء. واختاره أبو حاتم لتأنيث الخافية

QASHANI:69:18-23/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:69:18-23/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:69:18-23/r1.claim: People are presented before God with the inward forms of their deeds and actions.
QASHANI:69:18-23/r1.anchor: على الله بما في أنفسكم من هيئات الأعمال وصورالأفعال

RAZI-FULL:v30p96#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p96#2/r1.speaker: المشبهة
RAZI-FULL:v30p96#2/r1.claim: The anthropomorphists argue that if God were not in the Throne, carrying it would be pointless; they appeal to the verse saying people will be presented, which they think requires God to be in the Throne.
RAZI-FULL:v30p96#2/r1.anchor: قالت المشبهة : لو لم يكن الله في العرش لكان حمل العرش عبثا

RAZI-FULL:v30p96#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p96#2/r2.speaker: أهل التوحيد
RAZI-FULL:v30p96#2/r2.claim: The people of divine oneness reject a literal sitting: if God were in the Throne, the angels carrying it would carry God, implying divine need and greater angelic power, an explicit form of unbelief.
RAZI-FULL:v30p96#2/r2.anchor: لا يمكن أن يكون المراد منه أن الله جالس في العرش وذلك لأن كل من كان حاملا للعرش كان حاملا لكل ما كان في العرش

RAZI-FULL:v30p96#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p96#2/r3.speaker: أهل التوحيد
RAZI-FULL:v30p96#2/r3.claim: They interpret such descriptions through familiar human customs: God appoints a house for visitation without inhabiting it, a stone as His right hand on earth, and record-keeping angels without being subject to forgetfulness.
RAZI-FULL:v30p96#2/r3.anchor: فخلق لنفسه بيتا يزورونه ، وليس أنه يسكنه ، تعالى الله عنه

RAZI-FULL:v30p96#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p96#2/r4.speaker: أهل التوحيد
RAZI-FULL:v30p96#2/r4.claim: Likewise, the Throne, angels around it, and the assembly at judgment follow the custom of a king sitting with attendants to judge officials; God neither sits on nor needs the Throne.
RAZI-FULL:v30p96#2/r4.anchor: أحضر الله يوم القيامة عرشا وحضرت الملائكة وحفت به ، لا لأنه يقعد عليه

STUDYQURAN:69:18/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:69:18/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:69:18/r1.claim: Tuʿraḍūn can mean either that people are exposed or brought forth, as in the verse about being brought before their Lord.
STUDYQURAN:69:18/r1.anchor: You shall be exposed translates tuʿraḍūn, which could also be rendered

STUDYQURAN:69:18/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:69:18/r2.speaker: IK, Q, R, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:69:18/r2.claim: A hadith describes three arraignments on Resurrection Day: people argue and make excuses at the first two; at the third, scrolls are handed out, with some receiving them in the right hand and others in the left.
STUDYQURAN:69:18/r2.anchor: some will take with their right hand and others will take with their left” (IK, Q, R, Ṭ)

STUDYQURAN:69:18/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:69:18/r3.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:69:18/r3.claim: The phrase may mean nothing is hidden from God, as another verse says of the Day people come forth.
STUDYQURAN:69:18/r3.anchor: nothing is hidden from God, as in 40:16, the Day when they come forth with naught concerning them hidden from God

STUDYQURAN:69:18/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:69:18/r4.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:69:18/r4.claim: R says the inner states and thoughts of people will be exposed, making believers rejoice and disbelievers grieve.
STUDYQURAN:69:18/r4.anchor: the inner states and thoughts of human beings will now be known, and the result will be that the believers will rejoice and the disbelievers will grieve (R)

STUDYQURAN:69:18/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:69:18/r5.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:69:18/r5.claim: Q offers the translation “None among you shall be hidden,” meaning that no person can escape God's Judgment.
STUDYQURAN:69:18/r5.anchor: None among you shall be hidden” (Q), meaning that no human being can evade God’s Judgment

TAB-FULL:v23p231/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p231/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p231/r1.claim: On that day, people will be presented before their Lord.
TAB-FULL:v23p231/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {يومئذ تعرضون لا تخفى منكم خافية} [الحاقة: 18] ذكر لنا أن نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقول

TAB-FULL:v23p231/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p231/r2.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري
TAB-FULL:v23p231/r2.claim: Abu Musa reports three presentations: the first two involve argument and excuses, and at the third the records fly into people's hands, some taking them in the right and others in the left.
TAB-FULL:v23p231/r2.anchor: عن الحسن، عن أبي موسى الأشعري، قال: «تعرض الناس ثلاث عرضات

TAB-FULL:v23p231/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p231/r3.speaker: عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v23p231/r3.claim: Abdullah reports three presentations on the Resurrection: the first two involve excuses and disputes; at the third the records fly into people's hands.
TAB-FULL:v23p231/r3.anchor: عن أبي وائل، عن عبد الله، قال: " يعرض الناس يوم القيامة ثلاث عرضات

TAB-FULL:v23p231/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p231/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
TAB-FULL:v23p231/r4.claim: Qatada transmits the Prophet's statement that three presentations occur, with disputes and excuses in the first two and records flying into hands at the third.
TAB-FULL:v23p231/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {يومئذ تعرضون لا تخفى منكم خافية} [الحاقة: 18] ذكر لنا أن نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يقول

SULAMI:v2p347#5/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p347#5/r1.speaker: محمد بن حامد
SULAMI:v2p347#5/r1.claim: Muhammad ibn Hamid calls heedless the person who neglects the great presentation, when limbs testify to their deeds; one who does not prepare, amend the self, and persistently supplicate over past failings is drowned in heedlessness.
SULAMI:v2p347#5/r1.anchor: قال محمد بن حامد : الغافل من غفل عن العرض الأكبر حين تشهد على العبد جوارحه لا شاهد عليه إلا منها

TUSTARI:69:18/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:69:18/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:69:18/r1.claim: People are presented before God and judged for their deeds; nothing is hidden, all is recorded in prior knowledge, and they are asked about everything.
TUSTARI:69:18/r1.anchor: أي تعرضون على الحق عز وجل، فيحاسبكم بأعمالكم، لا يخفى عليه

TUSTARI:69:18/r2.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:69:18/r2.speaker: author
TUSTARI:69:18/r2.claim: God's questioning about favors includes whether one recognized the hours and gatherings granted for His sake and whether He answered a request for a wife; if He asks about such favors, how will He question about disobedience?
TUSTARI:69:18/r2.anchor: ألم تكن عارفا بالساعات من أجلي؟ ألم يوسع لك حتى في المجالس

TUSTARI:69:18/r3.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:69:18/r3.speaker: عتبة الغلام
TUSTARI:69:18/r3.claim: ʿUtba the ascetic says a believing servant may be held before God over a single sin for a hundred years.
TUSTARI:69:18/r3.anchor: وقد حكي عن عتبة الغلام أنه قال: إن العبد المؤمن ليوقف

TABATABAI:69:18-19/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:69:18-19/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:69:18-19/r1.claim: Being presented means being shown before God for judgment, like a seller spreading goods before a buyer.
TABATABAI:69:18-19/r1.anchor: والعرض إراءة البائع سلعته للمشتري ببسطها بين يديه

TABATABAI:69:18-19/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:69:18-19/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:69:18-19/r2.claim: On that day people's beliefs and deeds are exposed so fully that nothing remains hidden: the unseen becomes witnessed and secrets public.
TABATABAI:69:18-19/r2.anchor: إبراز ما عند الإنسان من اعتقاد وعمل إبرازا لا يخفى معه عقيدة خافية ولا فعلة خافية وذلك بتبدل الغيب شهادة والسر علنا

TABATABAI:69:18-19/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:69:18-19/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:69:18-19/r3.claim: God's exclusive dominion, command, and knowledge, and creation's exposure before Him, are always true; the Day makes them unmistakably manifest.
TABATABAI:69:18-19/r3.anchor: كل ذلك دائمية الثبوت له تعالى، وإنما المراد ظهور هذه الحقائق يومئذ ظهورا لا ستر عليه ولا مرية فيه

TABRISI:69:18-24/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:69:18-24/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:69:18-24/r1.claim: On Judgment Day all morally responsible people are exposed before God.
TABRISI:69:18-24/r1.anchor: يعني يوم القيامة تعرضون معاشر المكلفين

TABRISI:69:18-24/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:69:18-24/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:69:18-24/r2.claim: Nothing hidden from you remains hidden: the phrase can mean a hidden person, a hidden deed, or the verbal noun of anything hidden.
TABRISI:69:18-24/r2.anchor: أي نفس خافية أو فعلة خافية

TABRISI:69:18-24/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:69:18-24/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود وقتادة
TABRISI:69:18-24/r3.claim: Ibn Masud and Qatada report three presentations of creation: two with excuses and disputes, then a third when records fly into the hands, right or left.
TABRISI:69:18-24/r3.anchor: وروي في الخبر عن ابن مسعود وقتادة أن الخلق يعرضون ثلاث عرضات اثنتان فيها معاذير وجدال

TABRISI:69:18-24/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:69:18-24/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:69:18-24/r4.claim: God does not expose creation to learn what He did not know; He knows all their deeds by His essence and exposes them so creation can see them.
TABRISI:69:18-24/r4.anchor: وليس يعرض الله الخلق ليعلم من حالهم ما لم يعلمه فإنه عز اسمه العالم لذاته يعلم جميع ما كان منهم

FARRA:v3p181/r3.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p181/r3.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p181/r3.claim: Yahya ibn Waththab reads masculine لا يخفى; the others read feminine لا تخفى. Both are sound, like the paired forms “the cry seized” and “the cry seized [them].”
FARRA:v3p181/r3.anchor: قرأها يحيى بن وثاب بالياء، وقرأها الناس بعد- بالتاء- (لا تخفى) ، وكل صواب، وهو مثل قوله: «وأخذ الذين ظلموا الصيحة » . وأخذت.

THALABI:v10p29#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p29#2/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p29#2/r1.claim: The Kufans except ʿĀṣim read with yāʾ; the remaining readers use tāʾ.
THALABI:v10p29#2/r1.anchor: بالياء كوفي غير عاصم والباقون بالتاء منكم خافية

THALABI:v10p29#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p29#2/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p29#2/r2.claim: A hadith describes three Judgment Day presentations: two for disputes and excuses, then one when records fly into hands, some taking them right-handed and others left-handed.
THALABI:v10p29#2/r2.anchor: يعرض الناس يوم القيامة ثلاث عرضات، فأما عرضتان فجدال وخصومات

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p161/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p161/r1.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p161/r1.claim: People are presented before God for their reckoning, and nothing about them is hidden.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p161/r1.anchor: قوله: {يومئذ تعرضون} قال مقاتل: تعرضون على الله لحسابكم، فلا يخفى منكم خافية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p161/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p161/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p161/r2.claim: Through ʿAṭāʾ, Ibn ʿAbbās explains that no hidden act or trait is concealed from God.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p161/r2.anchor: قول عطاء، عن ابن عباس: لا يخفى منكم على الله فعلة خافية، وخصلة خافية

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p161/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p161/r3.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p161/r3.claim: Al-Kalbī says no deed is hidden from God; he also gives the sense that no person is hidden from Him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p161/r3.anchor: ونحو ذلك ذكر الكلبي، فقال: يقول: لا تخفى على الله من أعمالكم شيء (¬9)، ثم قال: ويقال: لا يخفى على الله أحد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p161/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p161/r4.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p161/r4.claim: Maqātil’s alternative wording means that no righteous or wicked person is hidden when people are presented.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p161/r4.anchor: وهو معنى قول مقاتل: لا يخفى # الصالح ولا الطالح (¬1) إذا عرضتم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p161/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p161/r5.speaker: قراءة العامة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p161/r5.claim: The general reading uses the feminine tāʾ in takhfā.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p161/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p161/r6.speaker: أبو عبيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p161/r6.claim: Abū ʿUbayd prefers the masculine yāʾ reading, also read by Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī: yāʾ can suit masculine or feminine, whereas tāʾ suits only feminine, and the subject is separated from the verb by minkum.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p161/r6.anchor: واختار أبو عبيد الياء (¬4)، وهو قراءة حمزة، والكسائي (¬5)، قال (¬6): لأن الياء تجوز للذكر (¬7) والأنثى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p161/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p161/r7.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p161/r7.claim: Exegetes say people undergo three presentations on Judgment Day: the first two involve disputation and excuses, while in the third the records fly into people’s hands.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p161/r7.anchor: قال المفسرون (¬8): يعرض الناس يوم القيامة ثلاث عرضات، فأما # عرضتان فجدال ومعاذير

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:69:15-21/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:69:15-21/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:69:15-21/r5.claim: People will be presented before their Lord.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:69:15-21/r5.anchor: يومئذ تعرضون } على ربكم { لا تخفى منكم خافية

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:69:15-21/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:69:15-21/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:69:15-21/r6.claim: Nothing about them is hidden from God, as the cited wording says.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:69:15-21/r6.anchor: لا تخفى منكم خافية } كقوله: لا يخفى على الله منهم شيء

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:13/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:13/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:13/r1.claim: Sūr is a horn-shaped tube that sounds when blown; traditional Islamic belief holds that Israfil blows it twice, first killing all living beings and then raising them again.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:13/r1.anchor: Sözlükte sûr, “üflendiğinde ses çıkaran boynuz biçiminde bir boru” diye tarif edilir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:13/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:13/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:13/r2.claim: The scenes in verses 13–18 connect to and explain verses 1–3, describing how the Resurrection occurs and worldly life ends.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:13/r2.anchor: Kıyamet sahnelerini tasvir eden bu ayetler, 1-3. âyetlerle bağlantılı olup onları açıklamakta

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:13/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:13/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:13/r7.claim: For the term ʿarsh, discussed earlier in the Qurʾan, the commentary refers especially to al-Aʿraf 7:54.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:13/r7.anchor: Arş kelimesi daha önce birçok âyette geçmiş ve hakkında gereken açıklamalar yapılmıştır (özellikle bk. A‘râf 7/54)

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:13/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:13/r8.speaker: Müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:13/r8.claim: The Qurʾan does not explain the eight who carry the Throne; commentators infer from context that they are eight angels or carriers called the Throne-bearers, while others suggest eight persons, eight ranks, or eighty angels.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:13/r8.anchor: Müfessirler âyetin bağlamını dikkate alarak bu ifadeyi yukarıda anlatılan meleklerin üstünde, kendilerine “hamele-i arş” (arşın taşıyıcıları) denilen sekiz melek veya sekiz taşıyıcı olarak yorumlamışlardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:13/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:13/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:13/r9.claim: The author’s translation prefers the interpretation that the eight are angels; al-Razi instead prefers eight persons.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:13/r9.anchor: Biz, meâlde “sekiz melek” yorumunu tercih ettik; Râzî ise “sekiz şahıs” ifadesini tercih etmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:13/r10.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:13/r10.speaker: Cehmiye, Mu‘tezile ve Sünnî ulemânın önemli bir kısmı
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:13/r10.claim: These theologians interpret the Throne as dominion, meaning the whole universe, and its bearers as angels tasked with the universe’s operation; the material realm may collapse while God’s rule and order in other realms continue.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:13/r10.anchor: Cehmiye ve Mu‘tezile âlimleriyle Sünnî ulemâsının önemli bir kısmı, arş kelimesini “mülk” yani bütünüyle âlem olarak yorumlamışlardır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:13/r11.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:13/r11.speaker: İmam Ebû Hanîfe, Eş‘arî ve Mâtüridî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:13/r11.claim: Because these verses are among the ambiguous passages, these scholars say one should accept their wording as it is and regard not knowing its meaning as the soundest position.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:13/r11.anchor: İmam Ebû Hanîfe, Eş‘arî ve Mâtüridî gibi âlimler bu âyetler müteşâbihattan olduğu için ifadeyi aynen kabul etmemiz gerektiğini

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:13/r12.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:13/r12.speaker: İbn Âşûr ve Esed
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:13/r12.claim: Since God is beyond time and space, the angels carrying His Throne at the Resurrection can be read as a sign of the full and decisive manifestation of divine power on the Day of Judgment.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:69:13/r12.anchor: Allah zamandan ve mekândan münezzeh olduğu için kıyamet gününde meleklerin O’nun arşını taşıması olayı, “Allah’ın kudretinin hesap günündeki tam ve kesin tezahürünün işareti” olarak yorumlanmıştır

TABRISI:69:12/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:69:12/r2.speaker: حمزة
TABRISI:69:12/r2.claim: Hamza and al-Kisaʾi read lā yakhfā with yāʾ, while the other readers use tāʾ; both readings are sound.
TABRISI:69:12/r2.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي لا يخفى بالياء والباقون بالتاء.

ELMALILI:69:18-29/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:69:18-29/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:69:18-29/r1.claim: The presentation before God is a metaphor for accounting, likened to a ruler reviewing his army.
ELMALILI:69:18-29/r1.anchor: Burada “arz” hesabdan mecaz olup bir hükümdara askerinin ahvâlini görmesi için arzolunmalarına teşbih tarîkiyle ifade olunmuştur.

ELMALILI:69:18-29/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:69:18-29/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:69:18-29/r2.claim: This is not merely an outward presentation like worldly reviews: no hidden matter remains concealed, as 14:48 also describes.
ELMALILI:69:18-29/r2.anchor: Öyle arzolunursunuz ki gizli bir hâliniz kalmaz وَبَرَزُوا۟ لِلَّهِ ٱلْوَٰحِدِ ٱلْقَهَّارِ

ELMALILI:69:18-29/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:69:18-29/r3.speaker: Ebû Mûsâ el-Eş‘arî
ELMALILI:69:18-29/r3.claim: The Prophet says people are presented three times on Judgment Day: the first two involve disputation and excuses; at the third, pages fly into their hands.
ELMALILI:69:18-29/r3.anchor: Ebû Mûsâ el-Eş‘arî radıyallahu anh’tan rivayet [5327] etmişlerdir ki Resûlullah sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem şöyle buyurdu

NAHHAS:v5p21/r8.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p21/r8.speaker: الكوفيون
NAHHAS:v5p21/r8.claim: The agreement follows feminine form; Kufans read يخفى because the feminine is non-literal and separated from its verb.
NAHHAS:v5p21/r8.anchor: على تأنيث اللفظ وقراءة الكوفيين ( يخفى ) لأنه تأنيث غير حقيقي

NASHR:v2p389/r10.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p389/r10.speaker: حمزة، والكسائي، وخلف
NASHR:v2p389/r10.claim: Hamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Khalaf use the masculine yāʾ form; the others use feminine tāʾ.
NASHR:v2p389/r10.anchor: لا تخفى فقرأ حمزة، والكسائي، وخلف بالياء على التذكير، وقرأ الباقون بالتاء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p359#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p359#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p359#2/r1.claim: The address that people are presented encompasses all creation.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p359#2/r1.anchor: الخطاب في قوله تعالى: تعرضون لجميع العالم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p359#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p359#2/r2.speaker: أبو موسى الأشعري وابن مسعود
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p359#2/r2.claim: Abu Musa and Ibn Masʿud report two presentations involving excuses, accounting, disputes, and argument, followed by a third when books fly to right and left hands.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p359#2/r2.anchor: وروي عن أبي موسى الأشعري وابن مسعود أن في القيامة عرضتين فيهما معاذير وتوقيف وخصومات وجدال، ثم تكون عرضة ثالثة تتطاير فيها الصحف بالأيمان والشمائل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p359#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p359#2/r3.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وعلي بن أبي طالب وابن وثاب وطلحة والأعمش وعيسى
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p359#2/r3.claim: These readers use the masculine يخفى.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p359#2/r3.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي: «لا يخفى» بالياء وهي قراءة علي بن أبي طالب وابن وثاب وطلحة والأعمش وعيسى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p359#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p359#2/r4.speaker: الباقون
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p359#2/r4.claim: The other readers use the feminine تَخْفَى, agreeing with the feminine noun خافية.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p359#2/r4.anchor: وقرأ الباقون: بالتاء على مراعاة تأنيث خافية وهي قراءة الجمهور

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p359#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p359#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p359#2/r5.claim: Khafiya means an inner thought or conviction.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p359#2/r5.anchor: وقوله تعالى: خافية معناه ضمير ولا معتقد

JISHUMI:v10p7056/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7056/r12.speaker: عاصم والكسائي
JISHUMI:v10p7056/r12.claim: ʿĀṣim and al-Kisāʾī read يخفى with yāʾ because the verb precedes its subject; others read تَخْفَى with tāʾ agreeing with feminine خافية.
JISHUMI:v10p7056/r12.anchor: قرأ عاصم والكسائي: يخفى بالياء لتقدم الفعل على الاسم، الباقون: بالتاء لتأنيث (خافية).

JISHUMI:v10p7057/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7057/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7057/r4.claim: Al-khāfiya derives from concealment, opposite to making something public.
JISHUMI:v10p7057/r4.anchor: والخافية: فاعلة من خفي يخفى خفاء، فهو خاف، والإخفاء: خلاف الإعلان.
